Each scale is its own figure. The chevron is the driven two-level population

$$
P(t)=\frac{\Omega^2}{\Omega_R^2}\sin^2\!\left(\frac{\Omega_R t}{2}\right)
\exp(-\Gamma t),\qquad \Omega_R=\sqrt{\Omega^2+\delta^2}.
$$

with $\Omega/(2\pi)=20\,\mathrm{MHz}$ and shot noise.
$\langle Z\rangle=1-2P$ uses a diverging scale.
Synthetic example, not a measurement. The page mode selects the matching figure.

## Screen

### Rabi chevron

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
from review import for_renderings, heatmaps, show

def heatmap(name):
    return next(fig for fig in heatmaps() if fig.layout.title.text == name)

for_renderings(lambda appearance: show(heatmap("Rabi chevron"), reading="screen", appearance=appearance))
```

### ⟨Z⟩ chevron

```{python}
#| renderings: [light, dark]
for_renderings(lambda appearance: show(heatmap("⟨Z⟩ chevron"), reading="screen", appearance=appearance))
```

## Analytical diverging field

The analytical function sin(x) cos(y) uses Plotly's native RdBu scale, centered
at the function's zero value.
